content.title: Venezuela rallies to beat Italy, setting up WBC final with USA: Live updates and reaction
content.text: Follow live reaction from Miami as Venezuelans make first World Baseball Classic finaleGleyber Torres celebrates with his Venezuelan teammates after reaching the WBC final for the first time Getty ImagesVenezuela beats Italy to make WBC finalVenezuela will face Team USA in the World Baseball Classic final, after it beat Italy at loanDepot Park in Miami tonight. With both teams aiming to reach a first WBC championship game, it was Italy who took a 2-0 lead after J.J. D’Orazio was walked with the bases loaded and Dante Nori added an RBI groundout in the second inning.Eugenio Suárez’s solo home run got Venezuela on the board in the fourth inning before a clutch seventh-inning rally decided the game, as Ronald Acuña Jr., Maikel Garcia and Luis Arraez each recorded RBI singles to turn the game on its head.The final takes place tomorrow, also at loanDepot Park.Follow the latest news, analysis and reaction from our team of reporters, below.Share your views: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPrediction: USA wins 2026 WBC Getty ImagesU.S. 7, Venezuela 1Team USA tees off against a tired Venezuelan bullpen. No need for Mason Miller to pitch for the third time in five days. The power bats that were muted against the Dominican Republic put on a show in the WBC finale. Roman Anthony wins the WBC MVP award.Prediction: Venezuela wins WBC Getty ImagesVenezuela 6, U.S. 3The overall offensive numbers on Team USA aren’t awful. But a chunk of that is facing teams Brazil and Great Britain, whose arms aren’t largely MLB quality. For the most part, this lineup chock full of All Stars and Hall of Famers has struggled to put up crooked numbers. Venezuela’s pitching is a little beat up after a tight win over Italy, and has one fewer day to rest. But they still have a great bullpen and a good-enough lineup. They’ll have significant fan support in Miami, and have already slayed the defending champions. The USA will be the favorite, but Venezuela will take home the hardware.Who has the pitching advantage? Getty ImagesStarting pitching edge: Team USANeither of these starters was any good in their first outings of the WBC. Nolan McLean may well be the better pitcher, who will have the better season. But after allowing three earned runs in three innings, including two homers given up, it’s hard to say he has the edge. Then again, Eduardo Rodriguez allowed three earned runs over 2 ⅔ innings. Rodriguez has more experience. McLean might be the better pitcher right now. It’s close, but Rodriguez’s overall downward trajectory combined with his poor opening outing gives McLean the slight edge.Bullpen edge: VenezuelaThis will be all about availability. If Venezuela has their best arms available, they’re going to have the edge. If they don’t, Team USA, and their recent additions will make them fresher and better. If Team USA does not have David Bednar and Mason Miller, then they will be vulnerable at the back end of the game, particularly if Nolan McLean does not make a deep start. Venezuela’s available bullpen arms The Venezuelan bullpen has been nails in this tournament. The only downside for them is how heavily their best arms were worked in their semifinals win. In order to win tomorrow, some of their arms will have to pitch in back-to-back games — although that will probably be a question that loops in the players’ big league clubs. It will be interesting to see if Enmanuel De Jesus is available after pitching 2 ⅓ innings against Japan on Saturday. If Venezuela can’t go to some of its key relief arms, it will spell trouble.Team USA available bullpen arms So far, new bullpen additions Jeff Hoffman, Will Vest and Tim Hill have not made an appearance this WBC. That should change on Tuesday. Tyler Rogers, who pitched on Sunday, only needed two pitches to collect two outs, so he should similarly be available. It’s unlikely that DeRosa will call upon David Bednar once again, and it won’t be known until first pitch whether Mason Miller will be available to close.Still, there’s enough fresh arms that the U.S. should have enough to weather a potential bullpen game.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementComparing the starting pitchers Despite his availability, Minnesota Twins right-hander Joe Ryan will not get the start in tomorrow’s finale. In fact, he won’t pitch at all. That job belongs to Nolan McLean, who was tagged for three runs in three innings in his lone WBC start. MLB’s No. 8-ranked prospect, per Keith Law, has electric stuff but he might not be for long in the finale, particularly if any signs of trouble bubble over.Eduardo Rodriguez hasn’t been a very good big league pitcher since 2023 and had ERAs north of 5.00 over his last two years in Arizona. His expected stats based on quality of contact allowed have made him one of the least effective pitchers in MLB, all while batting a declining strikeout rate. In one game, anything can happen. But it’s a tough matchup against this particular U.S. lineup and the Venezuelans should be prepared to go to their strong bullpen early, if needed.Previewing Team USA’s lineup After shuffling things around against the Dominican Republic, manager Mark DeRosa will almost certainly ride the same lineup that put the United States in the championship game. Against the D.R., Gunnar Henderson got the start at third base, due in large part to his 7-for-9 career line against Luis Severino. That familiarity paid off as Henderson swatted a solo home run against Severino, one of only two runs scored by the U.S. He also made a few crafty plays at the hot corner, making it a no-brainer that he gets the start again in the final.Will Smith’s ability to navigate Team USA’s relievers through some tightrope acts, plus his remarkably better line so far this WBC, gives him the start again behind the plate. Otherwise, it’s business as usual for Team USA.Previewing Venezuela’s lineup Fun fact: Only two players in the Venezuela lineup have faced Nolan McLean during the Mets prospect’s brief MLB career. But the two that have, both have home runs. Ronald Acuña Jr. is 1-for-2 vs. with a homer, and Eugenio Suárez hit a homer off him in McLean’s big league debut.Then, there’s Luis Arraez, another Venezuelan player whose power has added an offensive element to their team. He has two in this WBC, and had two more in 2023 despite posting just 36 long balls total over his seven-year career. Maikel Garcia had a 5.8 WAR in 2025 and is one of the game’s best players, yet doesn’t get talked about enough. The Venezuelan lineup isn’t as deep or as powerful as that of Team USA, but there aren’t any major holes in it either.Head-to-head edge: USA vs. Venezuela Venezuela has an established big league hitter at every position in its lineup, including some very high-profile stars. But Team USA’s lineup is still superior at nearly every position. Just because most of the American stars are highlighted in this graphic however, doesn’t mean this is a lopsided matchup. Most of these were razor-thin choices that won’t necessarily make a difference in a one-game, winner-take-all scenario. Some of the top American stars, such as Aaron Judge and Bryce Harper, have been maligned for their inability to win the big game. Tomorrow is an opportunity for them to shift that narrative.Venezuela confirms WBC final starterEduardo Rodríguez, the longtime MLB pitcher now with the Arizona Diamondbacks, gets the start for Venezuela tomorrow, manager Omar Lopez confirmed postgame. He’ll be up against New York Mets rookie Nolan McLean, Team USA’s starter.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementJose Altuve’s reaction to the final out... and emotion from another former MVP in the stands, as well.How Ronald Acuña Jr. reacted to the final out...Pure emotion from the former National League MVP.Venezuela’s bullpen was perfect Getty ImagesItaly’s offense has been basically unstoppable throughout the WBC but Venezuela’s bullpen did not get that memo.After Keider Montero exited with the bases loaded and one out in the bottom of the second, Ricardo Sánchez came in and escaped the jam — only allowing one more run on a fielder’s choice. For the next seven innings Venezuela’s bullpen would not allow a single run, allowing just three hits and recording 21 outs. Here are the pitchers that participated in this dominant stretch:Ricardo Sánchez Luinder AvilaAngel ZerpaEduard BazardoAndrés MachadoDaniel PalenciaCervelli on Italy’s run Getty ImagesItaly manager Francisco Cervelli speaking after his team’s stunning World Baseball Classic run came to an end, translated from Italian:💬 “We are no longer the Cinderella and this is important: in three years, they’re going to take us seriously.”Venezuelan fans troll ItalySome good-natured fun from the joyous Venezuela fans in Miami.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore angles of the final outJust listen to the roar of the heavily pro-Venezuela crowd in Miami tonight. What a scene!Cervelli, Lopez embrace postgame Johnny Flores Jr./The AthleticA final moment between tonight’s semifinal managers, Francisco Cervelli of Italy and Omar López of Venezuela.Garcia: WBC final a ‘dream come true’Maikel Garcia grew up in La Sabana, Venezuela, a small coastal village, playing baseball with his cousins Ronald Acuña Jr. and Luisangel Acuña. Fast forward about 20 years, and all three are now in the major leagues, with Garcia and Ronald Jr. occupying the top two spots in the lineup of the first Venezuelan team to reach a WBC final …💬 “It’s a dream come true. I never been in a place like this and played the way I’m playing right now. It’s amazing. We want to bring the championship to the country ... Venezuela is a baseball country. We have to go out there and compete every single night, because they’re gonna get mad if we lose. “After this, I gotta play better in the big leagues. Big leagues are not like this. This is amazing, this is different. This is gonna help me play better in the big leagues.”Your views: Italy credit, Venezuela chance? Getty ImagesHere’s what you had for us in the discussion page as Venezuela made history against Italy to set up an enthralling WBC final with Team USA … 💬 David K: “Kinda surprised this is Venezuela’s first final. Nice run, Italy.”💬 Anon: “Was hoping Italy came out on top but I absolutely cannot complain, Venezuela was the better team tonight. Can’t wait for the matchup tomorrow night!”💬 Hillz A: “With Venezuela going up against Team USA’s bullpen game, will we have a first-time title winner by tomorrow night?!”Remember, you can join the discussion right here and you can always send your thoughts to us in an email too: live@theathletic.com
